requirements.statement: The platform shall allow XATA employees to create, manage, prioritize, track and complete personal and team TODO items.
The solution shall be a simple centralized web application that provides a common place to manage TODO items.
The platform shall allow users to quickly create and update TODO items.
The platform shall provide visibility of open, completed and overdue work.
The platform shall allow team members to assign TODO items to one another.
The platform shall provide basic priority and due-date management for TODO items.
The platform shall provide a simple dashboard for work tracking.
The first release shall be intentionally small and easy to use.
Users shall have user login and a basic user profile.
System shall allow an authenticated user to create a TODO.
A TODO shall contain title, description, status, priority and due date.
Users shall be able to edit TODOs they own or are authorized to manage.
Users shall be able to mark TODOs as completed.
Users shall be able to assign a TODO to another authorized user.
System shall support Open, In Progress and Completed statuses.
System shall support Low, Medium, High and Critical priorities.
Users shall filter TODOs by status, priority, assignee and due date.
Users shall search TODOs by title or description.
Users shall be able to view and delete TODOs.
Users shall be able to add optional notes to a TODO in addition to its description.
System shall provide a dashboard showing TODO status.
System shall provide a basic team view for assigned TODOs.
System shall retain audit information for TODOs, such as created date and updated date.
Employees shall create and manage their own TODOs, view assigned TODOs and update status.
Team Leads shall create and assign TODOs, view team TODOs and monitor overdue work.
Administrators shall manage users and basic platform configuration.
Dashboard shall show Open, In Progress, Completed and Overdue counts.
Team Leads shall view TODOs assigned to their team members.
System shall maintain created-by, created-date, updated-by and updated-date for TODOs.
Users shall be able to delete TODOs where permitted (priority: Should).
System shall prevent unauthorized modification of another user's TODO.
System shall provide a web interface through supported browsers.
Create TODO shall include entering a title.
Create TODO shall include entering a description.
Create TODO shall include selecting a priority.
Create TODO shall include selecting a due date.
Create TODO shall optionally allow assigning the TODO to a user.
Create TODO shall include saving the TODO.
Manage TODO shall allow viewing TODO details.
Manage TODO shall allow editing TODO information.
Manage TODO shall allow changing TODO status.
Manage TODO shall allow changing TODO priority or due date.
Manage TODO shall allow reassigning a TODO where authorized.
Dashboard shall include High/Critical priority TODOs.
A TODO must have a title.
A TODO due date cannot be earlier than its creation date unless explicitly permitted.
Completed TODOs must have Completed status.
Only authorized users can assign or modify TODOs.
A TODO is overdue when its due date has passed and its status is not Completed.
Deleting a TODO must not delete the user account or other TODOs.
Users can log in and create a TODO.
A TODO can be assigned, updated and completed.
Dashboard counts must correctly reflect TODO state.
Users cannot modify TODOs outside their authorization.
Filtering and search must return correct results.
The application must meet agreed NFRs.
XATA can complete the core TODO lifecycle without administrator assistance.
Normal page/API response time: ≤ 2 seconds for 95% of requests under normal load.
TODO create/update operation: ≤ 2 seconds for 95% of requests.
Dashboard loading: ≤ 3 seconds for 95% of requests.
Search/filter response: ≤ 2 seconds for 95% of requests.
Concurrent active users: at least 500.
Monthly availability shall be ≥ 99.5%, excluding agreed maintenance windows.
Planned maintenance shall be communicated at least 24 hours in advance.
Service shall be restored within 30 minutes after application failure.
The solution shall support growth in users and TODO volume without major redesign.
The solution shall support at least 100,000 TODO records initially.
Application services should be horizontally scalable where practical.
Database design shall support future growth beyond initial capacity.
All users shall be authenticated before accessing protected functionality.
Authorization shall be role-based.
Users shall only access TODO data permitted by their role.
Data shall be encrypted in transit using HTTPS/TLS.
Sensitive credentials shall not be hard-coded.
If passwords are locally managed, they shall use secure industry-standard hashing.
The application shall protect against common web vulnerabilities including injection, broken access control and XSS.
Administrative actions should be auditable.
TODO records shall have unique identifiers.
Required fields shall be validated server-side.
Updates shall not silently overwrite conflicting data.
Created/updated timestamps shall be stored consistently.
Referential integrity shall be maintained between TODOs and users.
Deleted data shall be handled in accordance with XATA's retention policy.
Core create/update/complete flow should require minimal steps.
UI shall be responsive for standard desktop and tablet screens.
Validation errors shall be understandable.
Status, priority and overdue items shall be visually distinguishable.
Common actions shall be discoverable without technical knowledge.
Target WCAG 2.1 AA principles where practical.
Keyboard navigation should support core workflows.
Form controls should have meaningful labels.
Text should have sufficient contrast and readable sizing.
Solution shall use modular, maintainable code.
Business logic shall be separated from presentation and persistence.
APIs and major components shall be documented.
Automated unit tests shall cover critical business logic.
Configuration shall be externalized from source code.
Logging shall support troubleshooting without exposing sensitive information.
Application errors shall be logged with sufficient troubleshooting context.
Health checks shall be available.
Key metrics should include request failures and response latency.
Logs should include correlation/request identifiers where appropriate.
Operational alerts should be configurable for service failures.
Production data shall be backed up according to an agreed schedule.
Backups shall be protected from unauthorized access.
Solution shall support restoration after major failure.
Target RPO is 15 minutes unless XATA agrees otherwise.
Target RTO is 30 minutes.
Solution shall support current versions of major enterprise browsers such as Chrome and Edge.
Browser-specific functionality shall be avoided unless approved.
APIs should use documented, versionable interfaces.
Solution shall collect only data required for TODO management.
Access to personal/team information shall follow XATA authorization rules.
Sensitive information shall not be written to application logs.
Data retention and deletion shall follow XATA policy.
Critical application/database components shall have documented recovery procedures.
Recovery procedures shall be tested periodically.
XBS shall document dependencies required to restore the service.
XBS shall demonstrate compliance with agreed NFRs through appropriate testing, evidence, configuration review and operational validation before production acceptance.
Security NFR category has Must priority.
Performance NFR category has Must priority.
Availability NFR category has Must priority.
Data Integrity NFR category has Must priority.
Backup & Recovery NFR category has Must priority.
Usability NFR category has Must priority.
Maintainability NFR category has Must priority.
Accessibility NFR category has Should priority.
Advanced observability NFR category has Should priority.

open_questions.question: What response time or effort qualifies as 'quickly' for creating and updating TODO items?
What is the scope of 'basic' priority and due-date management (for example, priority levels, due-date rules, reminders, or notifications)?
How is an item classified as 'overdue', and what content and behavior is expected from the 'simple dashboard' for work tracking and team workload visibility?
How are 'team' and team membership defined, and what rules govern assigning TODO items between team members?

The supplied evidence contains no explicit non-functional requirements (for example security, authentication, availability, performance, or accessibility). Are any such requirements applicable, and what measurable criteria define 'easy to use' for the first release?
BR-003 and BR-005 depend on 'authorized to manage' and 'authorized user', but the source does not define how authorization is determined or which roles hold it.
The source does not define 'overdue' for the Team Lead's monitoring responsibility, such as the threshold or the time basis for determining overdue work.
The scope of the 'basic team view', the 'basic user profile' and the 'basic platform configuration' is not defined; the source does not state which fields, settings or actions are included.

The supplied evidence contains no non-functional requirements (for example performance, security, availability or accessibility). Confirm whether NFRs exist elsewhere or are out of scope for this inventory.
What are the criteria for a TODO to be classified as Overdue, and how is the due date comparison defined?
Who is authorized to delete, reassign, or modify TODOs? The BRD uses 'where permitted' (BR-013) and 'where authorized' (Manage TODO), and does not define the permission or authorization rules.
Which browsers are considered supported for the web interface?
What are the allowed priority values, and how do High and Critical map to the priority selection?
How is team membership defined for Team Leads, and how is a Team Lead's team determined?
Does the dashboard 'Total open TODOs' figure equal the 'Open' count in BR-010, or is it a separate metric?
What exceptions permit a due date earlier than the creation date, and who is authorized to grant that permission?
What authorization model defines which users may assign, modify, or access specific TODOs?
What are the agreed NFRs that the application must meet? The NFR document is referenced but its content was not supplied in the evidence.

The supplied BRD evidence contains only an approval/governance statement and no explicit functional requirements. Are there BRD functional requirements that were not included in the supplied evidence?

NFR-PERF-001 and NFR-PERF-002 through NFR-PERF-004 refer to 'normal load' and '95% of requests' without defining the normal load profile, measurement window, or how the percentile is calculated. What defines normal load and how should these targets be measured?

NFR-PERF-005 does not define 'active users' or the time window over which concurrency is measured, and it does not specify the expected load condition in which 500 concurrent active users must be supported. How should concurrent active users be defined and measured?
What does 'without major redesign' mean in measurable terms, and what user count and TODO volume growth target applies?
What is the future capacity target beyond the initial 100,000 TODO records, and over what time period?
Under what conditions is horizontal scalability 'practical', and is 'should' a binding requirement or a preference?
Which maintenance windows are considered agreed, and who agrees them?
What roles exist, and which TODO data each role may access?
Under what conditions are passwords 'locally managed' versus externally managed, and which identity source applies?
Which web vulnerability standard or verification method applies to 'common web vulnerabilities', and does the list of injection, broken access control and XSS cover the full scope?
What administrative actions must be auditable, what audit data must be retained, and is 'should' a mandatory obligation?
What is XATA's retention policy for deleted TODO data, and where is it defined?
How should conflicting updates be detected and resolved, given that silent overwrite is prohibited but no resolution behaviour is specified?
What is the maximum number of steps or the target interaction measure for the core create/update/complete flow to count as 'minimal steps'?
Which specific 'standard' desktop and tablet screen sizes or breakpoints must the UI support for the responsiveness requirement?
Which actions are considered 'common actions' that must be discoverable without technical knowledge, and how will discoverability be verified?
Which WCAG 2.1 AA principles are in scope, and what criteria define 'where practical' as an exception to the target?
What measurable thresholds define 'sufficient contrast' and 'readable sizing' for text?
Which business logic is considered 'critical', and is there a required unit test coverage target?
Which key metrics are required, and what latency thresholds or measurement periods apply to response latency?
In which cases are correlation/request identifiers considered 'appropriate' to include in logs, and which service failures must trigger configurable alerts?
What is the agreed backup schedule, and who agrees it?
What constitutes a 'major failure' that the solution must support restoration from?
Under what process and by whom would XATA agree to a different RPO than 15 minutes, and how are RPO and RTO measured?
Which browser versions count as 'current', and which other browsers beyond Chrome and Edge are in scope as 'major enterprise browsers'?
Who approves browser-specific functionality, and what is the approval process?
How often must recovery procedures be tested ('periodically' is undefined), and which components are classified as critical?
What are the XATA authorization rules and XATA data retention and deletion policies that the solution must follow? These documents are not in the supplied evidence.
What does 'XBS' refer to, and is it the party responsible for documenting restoration dependencies?

The priority table assigns Must or Should to NFR categories but does not state the measurable NFR thresholds, units, or acceptance criteria for each category. Which agreed NFR values apply to each category?
The acceptance statement refers to 'agreed NFRs' but the evidence does not identify where the agreed NFR set is documented or which NFRs are in scope for production acceptance.
